small_guidance:
- Increase BLOCK_P (e.g. 256/512) and try num_warps=4 to reduce launch overhead; the grid is N*OC*ceil(PH*PW/BLOCK_P) = 128*64*72 ≈ 590k programs which is excessive.
- Replace the `tl.where(tap_mask, ...)` broadcast accumulation (POOL2×BLOCK_P scratch) with a direct scalar accumulator: since each (kh_idx,kw_idx) tap contributes to exactly one pooled output, just accumulate `pooled += x_val * w_val` directly (divide once at end), removing the POOL2 dimension and giving a huge register/compute reduction.
- Wrap configs in `triton.autotune` over (BLOCK_P ∈ {64,128,256}, num_warps ∈ {2,4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3}).
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an implicit-GEMM style kernel: one program per (N, pooled-tile), accumulate a full (BLOCK_OC × BLOCK_P) tile across all OC at once so the input loads are reused across output channels (currently every OC re-reads the same input window). With OC=64 a single program can hold all 64 channels in registers, eliminating ~64× redundant input loads.
- Fuse the OC-axis reduction (sigmoid + sum over channels and spatial) inside the same kernel so the per-(N, pooled-tile) program emits a single scalar atomic_add per N — fewer atomics and no intermediate writes.
- Drop the POOL2 accumulator dimension entirely: each input pixel maps to exactly one pooled output, so accumulate the conv result directly into a single (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_P) pooled tile, divide by POOL*POOL once, sigmoid, then reduce.
